correctness.rationale: In the specified symmetric payoff game with a-favoring ties, sample-k response is binomial tail m_k=ceil(k/(1+u)). For k≤4, divide F_{k,m}−p by p(1−p): h_1=0,h_2=1,h_3,2=2p−1,h_3,1=2−p,h_4,2=−3p²+5p−1,h_4,1=3−3p+p². The u<3 mixture is concave with h(1)=1−θ_1≥0, hence no positive-to-negative crossing at an interior zero when θ_1<1; θ_1=1 yields a zero field, not asymptotic attraction. When u≥3 all nontrivial terms strictly positive. Endpoints u=2,3 obey the stated threshold changes. For 1<u<3/2 and θ_2=α,θ_5=1−α, drift is p(1−p)[2α−1−(1−α)(6p³−9p²+p)]. The cubic has positive maximum M=7√7/18−1 at p_-=(3−√7)/6; two simple roots with +,−,+ drift precisely for 1/2<α<7√7/(18+7√7), with lower attracting, upper repelling, p=1 attracting, and a non-attracting fold at α_c. At α≤1/2 only a repelling interior crossing can occur. Independent exact rational calculations verified all binomial factorizations, α=0.503 root-sign brackets and both parameter-boundaries; infinite quantifiers rest on polynomial shape analysis.

originality.rationale: Arigapudi, Heller and Schreiber 2025 AEJ Microeconomics, arxiv:2305.10301v2, Theorem 1 rules out stable interior miscoordination under homogeneous samples and Theorem 2 gives heterogeneous stable interior examples for sufficiently disparate/larger samples; the published theorem does not specify the sharp universal budget five or that all k≤4 mixtures fail. Its formulas provide the model but do not directly give the algebraic first threshold and exact 2/5 interval. Oyama, Sandholm, Tercieux 2015 establish sample-best-response selection/dominance sufficient conditions, not this two-sided interior-stability minimality. Izquierdo & Izquierdo focus on pure equilibrium stability and different statistical inference; no same cutoff established in inspected primary. Resultary sampling-best-response semantic search returned other finite game/sample problems but not this theorem. An earlier derivation based on their published general response function is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed analysis of the Arigapudi et al. binomial field or an extension of older sample response stability lemmas might derive the same first attainable sample budget.
The model assumes favorable ties for action a, symmetric binary payoffs u>1, deterministic infinite-population ODE; no claims for finite stochastic games or other inference.
Finite root-sign checks are corroboration only; the concavity and cubic sign arguments establish universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: A universal minimum observation budget for persistent mixed behavior is a natural structural threshold in heterogeneous best-response population dynamics. The surprising necessity of five draws (not just sufficiency) and exact bifurcation window distinguish a persistent mixed attracting state from mere diversity of response rules, with an explicitly competing pure-state basin. This is more than a low-order expansion of a known simple game.

limitations: One-population symmetric two-action mean-field coordination model; payoff ratio u>1, ties favor a.
Nonexistence for all finite distributions with support <=4; explicit sufficiency requires 1<u<3/2 and support {2,5}.
Stability is dynamical population attraction, not mixed Nash equilibrium of stage game.
